web.description:
# The 9th AI City Challenge
###### Abstract
Track 1 focused on multi-class 3D multi-camera tracking, involving people, humanoids, autonomous mobile robots, and forklifts, using detailed calibration and 3D bounding box annotations. Both Track 1 and Track 3 datasets were generated in NVIDIA Omniverse.

## 1 Introduction
Multi-Camera 3D Perception: This task advanced multi-camera tracking into the 3D domain using a large-scale synthetic dataset generated via NVIDIA Omniverse.

## 3 Datasets
### 3.1 Physical AI Smart Spaces Dataset
The dataset features synchronized multi-camera scenes in a synthetic warehouse, with 2D/3D bounding boxes for various object categories including humans and mobile robots.

The Physical AI Smart Spaces Dataset [ [19](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.13564v1#bib.bib19)] is a large-scale synthetic dataset generated via NVIDIA Omniverse for multi-camera 2D/3D person tracking. It features over 250 hours of video across nearly 1,500 cameras deployed in diverse indoor environments such as warehouses, hospitals, and retail spaces.

The combined use of these extensions enabled the generation of diverse, high-fidelity synthetic scenes suitable for multi-camera tracking, occlusion handling, and spatiotemporal reasoning.

## 4 Evaluation Protocols
### 4.1 Track 1 Evaluation
Track 1 challenged teams to detect and consistently track 3D objects across multiple synchronized cameras in complex indoor environments [ [19](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.13564v1#bib.bib19)]. The dataset was generated with synthetic animated scenes using both the IRA and IRO extensions in NVIDIA Omniverse.

The dataset includes over 250 hours of synthetic video from 1,500 cameras with detailed 2D/3D annotations and cross-camera identities.

web.description:
## 2024 Data and Evaluation Method
**Track 1: Multi-Camera People Tracking**

_**Track 1: Multi-Camera People Tracking**_

Challenge Track 1 involves synthetic animated people data in multiple indoor settings generated using the NVIDIA Omniverse Platform.

Teams should detect and track targets across multiple cameras.

In this challenge track, teams will be ranked on the leaderboard based on their HOTA scores calculated using 3D distance measurements in a multi-camera setting.
